- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral (e.g., 0.00 or negative values), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for the next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., +1.00 followed by -0.33 or +0.67), model often overreacts; cap forecast at 1.5x the recent 7-day average to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative shifts (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or negative), model underestimates; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model tends to overforecast in early horizon (e.g., 1–5 days) when sentiment is positive; apply 10–20% downward adjustment for short-term (1–7 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment is positive but recent price is falling, model often fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average if sentiment > 0.5.
- If model forecast exceeds 3x recent 7-day average, flag as outlier; reduce by 50% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 10+ day forecasts, model often underestimates; add 0.1–0.4 to forecast if sentiment is positive and recent price is stable or rising.
